note: Added 2026-09-09 together with 13 sibling Greater Vancouver property tax notices, on request, to grow `propertytax` coverage from 6 documents to 20. City of Delta (5040 48 AVE), a mixed residential + business-class roll. total_invoice_amount is the COLUMN A (no home owner grant) figure: A=45,691.50 / B=45,121.50 / C=44,846.50 before arrears. ARREARS RULE, set 2026-09-09 by the user and implemented in the analyzer prompt (commercial-narrative-v20): on a PROPERTY TAX notice, unpaid arrears and delinquent taxes from prior years are still payable and ARE part of the amount due, so total_invoice_amount is the arrears-INCLUSIVE total. This REVERSES the general carried-forward rule, which treats a prior balance as already paid and remains correct for commercial and utility bills. Only three corpus notices carry non-zero arrears (this one, property_delta and property_north_van_city); notices whose only prior-period line is a PREPAYMENT credit (property_surrey, property_Vancouver2, property_north_van_district) are unaffected, because a credit already reduces what is owed. ARITHMETIC ON THIS PAGE: 'TOTAL CURRENT TAXES 45,691.50' + 'Outstanding Arrears Taxes (including interest to July 2) 2,318.27' = 'TOTAL OUTSTANDING TAXES 48,009.77', which is the asserted value. DO NOT 'correct' it back to 45,691.50 -- that is this bill's own charges only, and the earlier version of this note asserted exactly that before the rule changed. MEASURED: under the pre-v20 analyzer this read 45,691.50 on 12 of 12; under commercial-narrative-v20 it reads 48,009.77 on 3 of 3, on BOTH twins, routing HAPPY_PATH_CANDIDATE 3/3. billing_period IS asserted: the page prints 'For the period January 1 - December 31, 2026'. || invoice_date is NOT asserted: this notice prints no issue-date label, so build_write_values substitutes date.today() and the scaffold captured the run date -- a false green that would flip red the next day. Same reason as property_surrey. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free text that rewords itself every run. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume it for property tax. Observed behaviour: number_of_days_extract returns no value at all and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' (catalogued defect B3), which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to the period-derived 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design -- so the field flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20); it is critical on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA). || The narrative fields (diagnosis_solution, recommendation, warranty and their zh_hant twins) are blank by policy on a municipal bill. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label). The written value is the bare folio, which is what an owner quotes to the municipality.
